name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: We should adopt stake-weighted confidence drop thresholds for link coverage, as this approach allows us to prioritize high-stakes links and allocate resources effectively. By doing so, we accept the trade-off of potentially overlooking low-stakes links that may still be important, but this is justified by the increased focus on critical links that drive the most value. This decision aligns with our goal of pushing link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day, as it enables us to make targeted progress and maximize the impact of our efforts. By prioritizing high-stakes links, we can ensure that our progress is meaningful and contributes to the overall quality of our link coverage.

name: Scriv
text: The stake-weighted confidence drop risks gaming the metric—teams could inflate stakes to justify skipping low-confidence links, eroding the gate’s purpose. A better alternative: enforce a hard floor of 95% coverage for critical paths while applying stake-weighting only to the remaining 5%, ensuring the gate stays intact. Settle it by running a 48-hour pilot on a non-critical branch and measuring if the override rate stays below 2%.
